allow_large: The owner added UX items to this fix on 2026-09-27
done_when: PR titles are short (a task: story title: task name; a fix: the why's first clause, 70 characters at most), a promoted spec task's ID is SPEC, the PR body labels Why and Done when and the review block opens with a plain verdict and no hash, the board's GitHub call succeeds on this repo and links each item to its PR, and forge next says which items are ready to merge with their PR link and names the findings a close stopped on; tests through the real commands prove each; the board also lists active stories first, folds finished fixes into one collapsed line with their count, and uses plainer status words; existing tests that expect the old titles, IDs, PR body or output are updated to the new wording, since that change is deliberate

findings.body: The first clause supplied here is shorter than 70 characters. Removing `[:70]` from production would therefore leave this test passing, so the explicitly required length limit has no effective regression test. Exercise `forge close` with a first clause longer than 70 characters and assert the resulting title's exact content and length.
findings.title: Not done: command-level proof of the 70-character fix-title limit

findings.body: The stub returns the same successful response for every `pr list` request, and the assertion checks only the last request's limit. Restoring `files,statusCheckRollup` to the initial 1,000-PR query would leave this test passing while restoring the reported timeout trigger. Add an edge stub that rejects the expensive bulk request and returns distinct metadata/detail responses, then verify the real board command renders successfully with links.
findings.title: Not done: command-level proof that the board avoids the expensive GitHub query

findings.body: Only 25 PRs across all states receive files and checks, but downstream consumers still use the larger listing. `board.py:248–257` selects the last 25 merged PRs and treats missing files as no Forge changes; open or closed PRs occupying the detail window therefore cause undercounting. An older open PR also loses its green-check readiness through `board.py:215–223`. Fetch bounded details for the relevant open and merged PRs instead of silently treating omitted details as negative results.
findings.title: Fetch details for the PRs whose status and metrics the board displays

findings.body: After a clean review, `forge close` can stop because an additional check such as `lint` failed: `checks.py:38–50` includes checks outside the configured names and rejects failures. The saved status remains `waiting for checks`. This new path nevertheless announces 'ready to merge' when the named checks pass, because `board._green_at` examines only those names (`board.py:269–274`). Use readiness criteria consistent with close so a rejected item is not presented as ready.
findings.title: Apply close's check policy before announcing readiness

findings.body: This second read uses the platform's default encoding, whereas `review.task` already reads the same document explicitly as UTF-8 (`review.py:85–91`). On supported Python versions running Windows without UTF-8 mode, non-ASCII story text can produce a corrupted PR title or a `UnicodeDecodeError`, stopping close before PR creation. Reuse the text returned by `review.task`, or specify UTF-8 explicitly.
findings.title: Reuse the UTF-8 story text when extracting the title

why: Forge's pull requests and status output bury what the owner must do: titles run to 300 characters, promoted spec tasks get 40-character IDs, PR bodies and review blocks carry hashes and jargon, the board times out on GitHub and has no links, and forge next never says what is ready to merge or why a close stopped
